papers.title: Graphene oxide-engineered dental implants: orchestrating antibacterial defense and osteo-immunomodulation for enhanced osseointegration
papers.abstract: Dental implant technology has brought significant benefits to millions of patients with missing teeth, substantially improving their quality of life. However, titanium-based dental implants still face two stubborn problems—peri-implant infection and inadequate osseointegration, which seriously undermine their therapeutic outcomes and overall clinical success. To address these two key bottlenecks, this study developed a graphene oxide (Graphene oxide)-engineered dental implant endowed with synergistic antibacterial and osteoimmunomodulatory properties. This implant exhibited broad-spectrum antibacterial effects against three common pathogenic strains in dentistry by disrupting bacterial cell membranes and increasing intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels. Moreover, the implant regulated the macrophage polarization toward a pro-regenerative phenotype, thereby optimizing the local immune microenvironment and promoting the extension and differentiation of osteoblasts. In vivo studies confirmed that GO-engineered implants enhanced antibacterial defenses, promoted inflammation resolution, and accelerated osteogenic regeneration. These results suggest the preclinical potential of GO-based surface modification for dental implants. By integrating antibacterial, immunomodulatory, and osteogenic functions, this implant demonstrates promising preliminary performance in promoting early osseointegration and short-term local biological stability, offering a candidate strategy for further implant design.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究氧化石墨烯涂层牙种植体的抗菌与骨免疫调节，与用户关注的LPBF多孔植入物力学/应力遮挡方向关联较弱。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not involve LPBF fabrication, porous structure design, stress shielding, stiffness matching, or mechanical/fatigue testing; it is a surface-coating biological study on dental implants.

summary_zh.method: 通过氧化石墨烯表面改性构建兼具抗菌与骨免疫调节功能的牙种植体。

summary_en.motivation: Titanium dental implants remain limited by peri-implant infection and insufficient osseointegration, which compromise clinical success.
summary_en.method: A graphene oxide-engineered implant surface was developed to confer combined antibacterial and osteoimmunomodulatory activity.
summary_en.result: The modified implant disrupted bacterial membranes, elevated intracellular ROS, shifted macrophages toward a pro-regenerative phenotype, and enhanced osteogenic regeneration in vivo.
summary_en.validation: Antibacterial and cell assays were combined with in vivo animal implantation to assess osseointegration and local biological stability.
